questions.question: Insulin was administered in a patient with severe hyperglycemia. This drug will stimulate glucose uptake in all the following except:

suspectLines.text: In the liver, glucose transport is through GLUT 2, which is insulin-independent. Insulin-stimulated glucose uptake takes place in the heart, skeletal muscle, and adipose tissue through GLUT 4.

questions.explanation: In the liver, glucose transport is through GLUT 2, which is insulin-independent. Insulin-stimulated glucose uptake takes place in the heart, skeletal muscle, and adipose tissue through GLUT 4.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about glycolysis?

options.text: 2 ATPs are utilized in the pathway

suspectLines.text: The complete breakdown of glucose involves the Krebs cycle (TCA cycle), which occurs in mitochondria, and not glycolysis. Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm of all cells. A 6-carbon glucose is converted into 3-carbon pyruvate in a ten-step anaerobic pathway. RBCs lack mitochondria and completely rely on glucose for energy. Phosphofructokinase-1 is the rate-limiting enzyme in glycolysis and is involved in conversion of fructose-6-phosphate to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. The irreversible steps are catalyzed by hexokinase, PFK-1, and pyruvate kinase. Two ATP are utilized in glycolysis. Net ATP from aerobic glycolysis is 7 ATP. Inhibitors noted in the source include iodoacetate for glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, fluoride for enolase, and arsenite at the 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate kinase step, causing glycolysis to produce zero net ATP.

questions.question: All of the following statements about glucokinase are true in comparison to other hexokinases, except:

suspectLines.text: Glucose is the only cellular substrate that can be phosphorylated by glucokinase. Glucokinase has a higher Vmax and higher Km value than hexokinase, requiring a higher concentration of glucose for half saturation. Hence glucokinase functions only when intracellular glucose concentration is high, as immediately after a carbohydrate-rich meal. Compared with hexokinase: glucokinase is in liver and pancreatic beta cells, has high Km and high Vmax, is not inhibited by G6P, and is inducible. Hexokinase is in most tissues, has low Km and low Vmax, is inhibited by G6P, and is not inducible. The source notes that glucokinase can act on other hexoses such as fructose and mannose, but because its Km for these reactions is high, this is not significant; therefore the best option has been chosen as given in the source answer key.

questions.question: How many net ATPs are generated in aerobic glycolysis?

suspectLines.text: Net generation of ATP up to pyruvate in aerobic glycolysis is 7 ATP. Two ATP are utilized in the earlier steps catalyzed by hexokinase and PFK-1. ATP-producing steps include glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (5 ATP equivalent from 2 NADH), 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate to 3-phosphoglycerate (2 ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation), and phosphoenolpyruvate to pyruvate (2 ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation), giving 9 ATP produced and 7 ATP net.

questions.question: Where does the Rapoport-Luebering cycle occur?

suspectLines.text: The Rapoport-Luebering cycle (2,3-BPG shunt) occurs in RBCs. 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate is converted to 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate by bisphosphoglycerate mutase. 2,3-BPG is present at high concentration in RBCs and decreases hemoglobin affinity for oxygen, promoting oxygen release in hypoxia. 2,3-BPG is hydrolyzed to 3-phosphoglycerate. Because the phosphoglycerate kinase step is bypassed, no ATP is generated in that step; anaerobic glycolysis through this shunt yields no net ATP.
